findings: Every one of the 37 merges maps to a charter goal. The diffs I could read (T-0038, T-0040, T-0051 to T-0056) do what their titles say. The full suite passes offline on a copy of the repo: 490 passed.
No dependency was added in this window. pyproject.toml and uv.lock last changed on 2026-09-29, before T-0001. The only schema changes are new migrations 0002 and 0003; migration 0001 was not edited.

No sign that tests were weakened. The assertions removed in test history swap placeholder IDs (900000100001) for real 9-digit IDs or the new name-based flow. Several done-tests were added for G2, G3, G4 and G5.

Repeated failures, now resolved: T-0015, T-0016, T-0033, T-0039 and T-0048 were parked, mostly because the worker reported status=None. Each was re-issued in a narrower form (T-0049, T-0031, T-0050, T-0053, T-0051/T-0052) and merged. Watch for a recurring worker problem that leaves status unset.
Cost is high: 168 agent runs for 37 merges, about 4.5 runs per merge, $66.09, and 21 sandbox denials. The denials were not explained in the input, so their causes need a look.

T-0053 adds get_channels, which builds the real channels from the environment. Tests always override it with FakeChannel, so CI never contacts Telegram or ntfy, which is compliant. In production, 'send test message' will send one real message to the visitor's own linked channel, which is what G5 intends.

T-0052's label test renders today.html directly with a hand-built Request and calls the private helper _status_item. It does not go through the /today route. That is acceptable, but if the route changes the test may not notice.
Minor: T-0040 sets PENDEL_DATA_DIR in two separate fixtures, one of them autouse. This duplication is harmless.

T-0054 to T-0056 are idle work that matches roadmap items M7 to M9 exactly. The platform-change fixture is a real Hauptbahnhof RE20 recording (planned platform 1, actual 3), documented in the fixtures README. No gold-plating found.
digest: A good day. 37 tasks merged, and each one serves a goal in the charter. I read the code changes for the last eight and they match their titles. The full test suite passes offline on a copy of the repo: 490 tests. No new dependencies were added, no existing database migrations were edited, and no tests were weakened. All five goals now have tests that check their definition of done, and the README describes the visitor pages. The idle work (README, a check that every form field has a label, a real recording of a platform change) matches the roadmap and stays small. Two things to watch. Spend is high: 168 agent runs and $66 for 37 merges, plus 21 sandbox denials that should be looked into. Five tasks were parked, most because the worker never reported a status; all were re-issued in a narrower form and merged. The new 'send test message' button uses the real Telegram or ntfy channel in production, but tests always swap in a fake, so no messaging service is contacted. Drift score is 1, so the system is not paused.
